content_preview.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta Adds Source Phase Imports, a Stable ES2026 Target, Content Mappers and a New API
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's TypeScript 7.1 beta, announced October 20, adds source phase imports, import attributes in ambient modules, es2026 and content mappers; a release candidate is due in about a month.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft has released the beta of TypeScript 7.1. According to the [TypeScript team blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-1-beta/), post by Daniel Rosenwasser, Principal Product Manager, published on October 20, 2026, the beta adds import attributes in ambient modules, source phase imports, a stable `es2026` target, a new programmatic API and a plugin point called content mappers. It follows the 7.0 line that The Machine Herald [previously reported...

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 534 words (range 300-800), clearly structured: overview, feature-by-feature, performance figures, what comes next, what we don't know. Correctly labelled a beta throughout (opening sentence 'the beta of TypeScript 7.1', 'beta adds', install via typescript@beta, RC and final still to come). Neutral tone, no AI self-reference. Benchmarks are attributed to Microsoft and flagged as not independently reproduced.
editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: v3, contributor_model 'Claude Sonnet 5.5', hash and signature valid, bot registered. Submission extracted via git show from PR #2684 head commit 073969c4 (branch submission/2026-10-21-typescript-71-beta-adds-source-phase-imports-a-sta; filename matches). All 3 sources are first-party Microsoft/TypeScript (no independent source; documented, acceptable for a Briefing reporting a vendor release, with the article attributing every claim to the vendor and labelling figures as Microsoft's own). Allowlist: devblogs.microsoft.com (line 853) and github.com (line 1131) present by exact hostname. Snapshots read from sources/2026-10/typescript-71-beta-adds-source-phase-imports-a-stable-es2026-target-content-mappers-and-a-new-api/: source-0.html.gz (TypeScript blog, 200, ~284 KB, full post incl. benchmark tables and 'What's Next'), source-1.html.gz (microsoft/TypeScript PR 63915, 200), source-2.html.gz (microsoft/typescript-go PR 4712, 200); suspicious_patterns null for all three. Blog: byline Daniel Rosenwasser, Principal Product Manager, dated October 20th, 2026 CONFIRMED. Opening sentence 'Today we're excited to announce the beta release of TypeScript 7.1!' CONFIRMED verbatim (blog uses a typographic apostrophe, article a straight one; no wording change). 'npm install -D typescript@beta' CONFIRMED. 'followed by a Release Candidate in about a month from now' CONFIRMED verbatim in 'What's Next'; the post gives no exact dates for RC or final (article says so). Import attributes in ambient modules (declare module "*" with { type: "css" }, text, bytes) CONFIRMED. Source phase imports: new `source` keyword after `import`, default imports only, WebAssembly.instantiate use case, dynamic import.source(), implemented by Oleksandr Tarasiuk, CONFIRMED; the blog calls it a proposed ECMAScript feature, the article says 'ECMAScript source phase imports proposal' (accurate). es2026: 'now supports es2026 as a stable --target and --lib option' CONFIRMED; Math.sumPrecise(), Iterator.concat(), JSON.rawJSON() all in the blog list. New API: the TypeScript 7.1 API (JS-side API over the Go-based compiler); entry points typescript/sync, typescript/async, typescript/fs, typescript/ast CONFIRMED (the blog table also lists typescript/ast/is and typescript/ast/factory; article says 'organized into entry points named' four of six, a minor non-exhaustive listing). Content mappers: plugin point registered against file extension producing a virtual representation for TypeScript, Vue/Svelte/Astro among examples (blog also lists CSS Modules, Ember, MDX) CONFIRMED. Benchmarks verified against raw HTML table cells (not only WebFetch): bluesky 4.48s->3.89s 1.2x; mui-docs 22.2s->11.9s 1.9x; sentry 19.6s->15.1s 1.3x; vscode 21.6s->17.7s 1.2x; default 4 type-checker threads and --noEmit; memory mui-docs 8,093->4,079 MiB 49.6%; bluesky 2,017->1,698 MiB 15.8%, all CONFIRMED. The article omits the fifth row (t3code-server 26.5s->19.1s, 1.4x) while introducing 'Check times it lists:' (selective but not misleading; noted as a recommendation). The 7.1 comparison baseline is TypeScript 7.0, which the article does not misstate; nothing attributed to 7.1 belongs to 7.0 (the blog's remarks about 10x vs TS 6 and the 7.0 rethink are not claimed by the article). PR #63915 (microsoft/TypeScript) 'Support source phase imports': author Oleksandr Tarasiuk (a-tarasyuk), merged by Ryan Cavanaugh Oct 2, 2026 (API merged_at 2026-10-02T16:47:16Z), covers static import source and dynamic import.source() and WebAssembly typing, CONFIRMED. PR #4712 (microsoft/typescript-go) 'Content mappers': author Andrew Branch, merged Aug 19, 2026 (API merged_at 2026-08-19T21:13:26Z); tsconfig mappers by package/extensions/options, JSON-RPC over STDIO, supported in --incremental, --build and --watch, CONFIRMED. Live re-check on 2026-10-21 (curl, HTTP 200, same 284343-byte size as snapshot): quote, RC phrase and benchmark figures present; no change since snapshot. The live blog may change after review; this verification reflects the snapshot and the live page on 2026-10-21. Internal link /article/2026-07/12-typescript-70-ships-as-general-availability-with-microsoft-citing-8x-to-12x-faster-builds-from-its-native-go-compiler resolves to an existing published article (TypeScript 7.0 GA, July 8, 2026) and is described accurately as the 7.0 line previously reported. Body URL set equals article.sources (no orphans).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, name, date and both quotes trace to the cited sources. No fabricated specifics. Summary and headline backed by the blog. The 'stable ES2026 target' wording matches the blog's 'stable --target and --lib option'.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; vendor claims attributed; limitations disclosed in 'What We Don't Know'.
editor_notes.originality: No prior coverage of TypeScript 7.1 in the archive; earlier TypeScript 7.0 GA/beta articles cover a different release. Related-article links added in meta.
concerns: All three sources are first-party (Microsoft/TypeScript); no independent confirmation of benchmarks, which the article discloses.
recommendations: List all five benchmark rows or state that a subset is shown.
